---
title: F200 policy-v1 boolean-cap migration fixture
---

This disposable source-and-successor fixture prepares one protected F200 Base save from the exact published `more-infinite-research_4.0.20000.zip` archive. It covers the historical policy-v1 boolean-cap boundary only: the source earns a player disablement through the published controller, while a separately disabled foreign gear row remains an unowned sentinel. It is not a general migration, balance, multiplayer, performance, or release-qualification claim.

The source asset is the public GitHub `v4.0.0` F200 archive, SHA-256 `5C0E299D78C4EE545958448DAE48D87BE5FE1B959875D4CB93A264D95D3DB0AE`, 1,067,014 bytes. Its actual `prototypes/mir/runtime/maximum_level_control.lua` member is the 9,606-byte policy-v1 body with SHA-256 `687E2EB214C7097C1691562ECE206AA69FDE24194164A8EF33F48AF14405C0EA`, matching the archived `09eb` source body recorded in `spec/evidence/historical-boolean-cap-archive-metadata.json`. The fixture cannot read another mod's runtime storage. It proves the source transition through native player state from enabled to disabled after the two real labs; the boolean-ledger shape remains independently inspected source evidence.

The source uses cap two, earns exactly two real powered gear laboratory completions, observes the native player state disabled with the published visible presentation, then seeds 27% saved work. It also retains a separate foreign level-one gear row disabled and hidden with a 42% `braking-force-1` queue. The source freezes its live lab immediately after the second completion without clearing the consumed-input witness; completed-state and cold-reload checks read that inventory without recharging it. The source writes a server save only after that observed cap transition and then requires two read-only cold reload markers.

The F200 and direct F200-to-F210 successors are separate pending routes from that same protected source save. Their thin fixed-target `control.lua` wrappers load one shared successor body, while each staged archive projects that body alongside its target-specific metadata. Each binds the reviewed `a575a4198807b6aea9e26963e3d9970fc5c068ae` player tree `398c79c687d2bc662c976355ced1436201c43f11` through its profile: F200 `more-infinite-research_5.0.20000.zip` SHA-256 `8DB28D2DE45F26033B5F54E176902A3138A903AF0F4B48EAB6B9971466021B4F` and F210 `more-infinite-research_5.0.21000.zip` SHA-256 `7CE6A4DF78019F6B98237E638A1C927C5FDB538D4A1442EE22D846DD962DDCDC`. A caller still supplies the selected path through `MIRArchive` and `ExpectedMIRArchiveSha256`. Each route must restore only the player right proven by the source state, preserve the foreign disabled and hidden sentinel with its queue, freeze the stocked lab immediately after its single observed completion without clearing its input witness, write a server save, and pass two read-only cold reloads. Neither route is a native result.

F200 Base 2.0.77 defines these four science packs as one-durability tool items. Its successor observes each occupied matching stack as `(count - 1) + durability / 1`, not through `get_item_count` alone: after the protected 27% investment, the single real lab is expected to consume the remaining 73% of each unit, leaving a 27%-durability tool. Unlike F210's one-second acceleration, the F200 successor uses one unit at five seconds (300 ticks): the remaining 0.73 tool unit therefore spans 219 whole ticks at the guarded Base `lab.researching_speed = 1`, force `laboratory_speed_modifier = 0`, and empty lab-module inventory. The F210 successor retains its separate one-second whole-item count assertion. This is a fixture expectation for the next F200 retry, not a retroactive native pass; the actual engine must still confirm the duration and 0.73 consumption.
